sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r9/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 34 (check 33) and Internal Quality Checks row 34 (annotation E34: multiple verifiers are combined in one flow by design)
.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r9/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (Known false positives: one criterion covering a whole flow, checks 26/28/33)
evidence: Read all 28 criteria (2 gates, 16 functional, 6 polish, 4 visual). No criterion enumerates several requirements and then waives most of them. Each states a single conjunctive bar; multi-part criteria say so explicitly ('Both parts must hold; failing either fails this criterion', e.g. functional/judge.toml:52, 83, 129, 180, 232; 'All three parts must hold' :264). The main two-target risk in this format, a 'Fails if' list narrower than the numbered legs (e.g. wall_added_live :97 omits leg 1's M-11/M-13 positive control and the live-within-ten-seconds requirement), is resolved by the injected prompt: functional/prompt.md:32-33 'A criterion passes only if every numbered leg and every listed positive control holds; its "Fails if" line names the main failures but never excuses a leg it does not mention', with the same rule at polish/prompt.md:23-25. All conditional or alternative wording I found is a defined acceptance branch, not a waiver of something already listed: wall_every_route :66 (JUDGE-W3 is accepted if either refused or filed under its own M-13 parent, never in M-11 or another matter; the 'Fails if' at :67 matches); timer_changes :138/:140 (earlier-versions replay is conditional because the viewer is graded in edits_and_stale_edit, and the unconditional transcript/search checks for '2,400'/'4,200' still enforce deletion); edits_and_stale_edit :174, hold_scope_and_release :156 and persistence :276 ('if the request carries a version', 'if it offers one', 'if the app shows earlier versions', each backed by an unconditional replay or readback); wall_added_live :92 ('Sian's page may briefly change; that is fine', which covers only the intermediate wall/lift cycle before the graded legs); safe_formatting :191 ('a shortened quote or snippet is fine', with whatever is shown still required to be literal); delete_confirm (an in-page or browser dialog). The only explicit relaxation is visual matter_sidebar :27: 'If no matter shows an unread count when you look, judge identification and selection only and do not lower the score for absent counts'. It waives one of three anchor-5 features, and only under a stated, observable condition. Unread state after the functional and polish runs depends on order (Gwen opens M-11 and M-13 in later criteria), so the rule is a deliberate tie-breaker that gives one bar per observed state, not two competing targets. The constraints gate's 'does not grade roles, correctness, or feature completeness' (:35-36) limits scope and waives nothing it lists. Conforming-alternative probe: an app with no earlier-versions viewer is not double-penalised in timer_changes, and an app that files W3 under its own parent is not failed. Broken-app probe: an app that signs Sian out on walling still fails wall_added_live because of the prompt rule that the 'Fails if' line excuses nothing. This row is a source-text check, so no runtime evidence is needed.
